tasks.short: Review departmental finances and recommend budgets that balance support demand, staffing and service quality.

steps.what: Retrieve departmental actuals and commitments from the {ERP}.
Reconcile actuals against budget and staffing assumptions in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Interpret variances and test staffing or spending options in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Discuss service risks and spending priorities with the department manager.
Write the budget recommendation and its assumptions in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Validated scenario figures, agreed priorities and an approved recommendation template.
loop.output: A budget recommendation with source references and explicit assumptions.
loop.check: Insert figures deterministically; supervisor checks explanations, assumptions and service consequences.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported statements remain flagged for manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Calculations are deterministic, but the explanation must connect changing priorities and service risks.

steps.what: Review the recommendation with finance and approve the departmental budget input.

tasks.design: Configure a scheduled {ERP} extract and use deterministic rules on the {DATA_PLATFORM} to reconcile costs and calculate scenarios for a {BI} dashboard. An artefact generator drafts the recommendation in the {DOCS} using validated figures and a bounded writing loop. The department manager approves the budget input after discussion with finance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cost mappings, staffing assumptions and explanations sit in separate files. Reconciliation ownership is often unclear.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting interfaces and inexpensive custom calculation tools make reconciliation easier to build. A bounded writing loop can turn checked figures into a first draft.
tasks.still_hard: Allocations, vacancies and uncertain demand can make accurate calculations misleading. Budget tradeoffs and employment consequences require judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Understand which savings would damage service, challenge weak assumptions and negotiate credible tradeoffs.
tasks.altitude: The supervisor spends less time reconciling files and more time testing service and staffing options. Budget approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Explain recurring contact drivers that increase support workload.
reach.learn: Contact categorisation, demand sampling and the difference between avoidable demand and essential support.

evidence.claim: Reconciliation and scenario arithmetic can use deterministic rules; budget priorities require human judgement.
A government trial reported time savings on drafting, summarising, records and reports; it does not establish savings for budget planning.

assumptions: The supervisor contributes departmental budget input rather than approving the company budget.
The {ERP} supports scheduled reports or accessible exports.
Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured savings.
Build ranges are working-day estimates; consultation and access waiting times can extend delivery.
unknowns: Which costs, commitments and staffing assumptions the supervisor can access.
Whether cost centre mappings and allocation rules are maintained.
Who approves departmental budget input and subsequent spending.
Whether employee-level data would trigger additional consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Can existing {ERP} reports produce the required reconciliation without custom integration?
Which past budget changes reveal missing commitments or unreliable demand assumptions?
new_work: Maintain cost mappings and scenario assumptions.
Resolve reconciliation exceptions and stale source data.
Check generated explanations against approved figures.
Review access permissions and failed refreshes.

tasks.short: Design, deliver and evaluate support training, service improvements and fair performance criteria.

steps.what: Review recurring support issues and quality samples in the {HELPDESK}.
Review course completion and assessment results in the {LMS}.
Discuss whether gaps arise from skills, procedures, tools or workload.
Draft learning exercises, service changes and evaluation criteria in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Improvement brief, approved procedures, anonymised examples and training template.
loop.output: Draft exercises, service changes and observable evaluation criteria.
loop.check: Supervisor checks procedural accuracy, answer keys, accessibility and fairness of proposed criteria.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved policy or scoring questions go to the supervisor.
loop.why_not_simpler: New exercises and explanations must fit varied service situations; templates alone cannot supply the content.

steps.what: Approve the programme, evaluation criteria and protected learning time.
Assign approved learning and record enrolments in the {LMS}.
Coach staff through practice cases and discuss difficulties.
Evaluate outcomes in the {BI} and recommend programme changes.

tasks.design: Configure team-level gap reports in the {HELPDESK} and {LMS}, with outcome comparisons in the {BI}. A bounded writing loop creates exercises and programme drafts in the {DOCS}; approved assignments run through the {LMS}. People diagnose causes, approve criteria, coach staff and interpret results.
tasks.previous_blocker: Service evidence, learning records and staff observations are disconnected. Tailored practice materials take time to prepare.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting and learning workflows handle much of the administration. Bounded drafting makes tailored exercises cheaper to produce and revise.
tasks.still_hard: Service improvement is difficult to attribute to training. GDPR, EU AI Act requirements and national consultation rules need assessment if worker monitoring or AI evaluation is introduced; workplace emotion inference is prohibited.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when poor results reflect broken processes, build trust during coaching and choose fair measures of success.

ambition.what: Optional refresher clinics for returning support staff

tasks.altitude: The supervisor spends more time diagnosing service problems and coaching staff. They can propose focused learning trials; authority to change formal performance criteria remains unchanged.

reach.task: Create practice cases for common troubleshooting problems.
reach.learn: Diagnostic sequencing, safe test environments and technically correct answer keys.

reach.task: Test whether practice conversations match real customer difficulties.
reach.learn: Scenario facilitation and observable feedback without inferring emotions.

evidence.claim: Configured reporting and learning workflows can support programme administration; diagnosis and coaching remain human work.
Research measured about 15% more issues resolved per hour with support assistance, especially for less experienced staff; this does not prove a training-programme effect.

assumptions: Basic service reporting and learning records already exist.
Initial reporting uses team aggregates and human-selected quality samples, without automated worker scoring.
Returning staff choose refresher support without disclosing medical or other sensitive reasons.
Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates.
Build ranges include access and consultation effort; national processes can extend elapsed delivery.
unknowns: Which training, service and performance criteria the supervisor may change.
Whether quality samples and learning records can be linked lawfully.
Which national employee consultation or consent requirements apply.
Whether the organisation already uses AI for worker monitoring or evaluation.
Whether the {BI} and {LMS} are available to the supervisor.
research_questions: Which recurring issues are caused by missing skills rather than policy or tool failures?
Can existing {HELPDESK} and {LMS} reports answer the evaluation questions?
What comparison period would distinguish learning effects from changes in demand or staffing?
new_work: Validate exercises, answer keys and proposed criteria.
Maintain approved source procedures and retire stale materials.
Review aggregate results for misleading comparisons.
Manage learning assignments and accessibility exceptions.
Reassess consultation and legal requirements when evaluation methods change.

tasks.short: Understand labour-management agreements and determine their effects on support department operations.

steps.what: Check agreement updates and implementation notices received through the {EMAIL}.
Read current agreements and relevant provisions in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Version-controlled agreements, effective dates, scope metadata and a supervisor's operational question.
loop.output: A reading brief with quoted clauses, page references and unresolved applicability questions.
loop.check: Verify every quotation against the source; supervisor checks scope, exceptions and effective dates.
loop.stop: One retrieval pass and one correction; missing or conflicting sources produce an escalation, not an answer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Search finds clauses, but relevant obligations and exceptions are expressed across varied prose.

steps.what: Compare previous and current provisions in the {DOCS}.
Clarify disputed clauses and operational implications with the HR adviser.
Record operational implications and proposed changes in the {DOCS}.
Record the completed review and follow-up owners in the {HCM}.

tasks.design: Configure agreement-version alerts in the {DOCS} and review tracking in the {HCM} or {WORKFLOW}. A deterministic comparison generates change tables, while a bounded reading loop produces clause-linked briefs from approved documents. The supervisor and HR adviser resolve interpretation questions; proposed operational changes enter their existing approval process.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agreement versions, local arrangements and interpretation notes are difficult to search together. Reliable applicability requires more than finding matching words.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned document stores, text comparison and source-linked reading loops reduce preparation work. They do not resolve legal ambiguity.
tasks.still_hard: Agreement scope, local arrangements and national employment rules can conflict or require specialist interpretation. GDPR applies to employee information; summaries must not silently become employment decisions.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise ambiguous consequences, ask the right questions and judge when an issue needs HR, legal or employee-representative involvement.
tasks.altitude: The supervisor spends less time locating clauses and more time understanding their operational consequences. Decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Answer routine staff questions about published working arrangements.
reach.learn: Agreement scope, effective dates, source citation and escalation boundaries.

evidence.claim: Version tracking and document comparison can reduce preparation without automating agreement interpretation.
A service-management product drafts answers and knowledge items for human approval; this supports the drafting pattern, not legal interpretation accuracy.

assumptions: HR maintains authoritative agreement versions and applicability information.
The {HCM} has a review record or the {WORKFLOW} can provide one.
The comparison uses text-readable documents with stable clause identifiers or aligned sections.
This task informs changes; it does not itself approve rosters, pay or employment terms.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are estimates.
unknowns: Which agreements and local arrangements cover the department.
Who provides authoritative interpretation and approves operational changes.
Whether agreement documents contain restricted or sensitive employee information.
Which national consultation requirements apply to the proposed document workflow.
Whether review completion is currently recorded in the {HCM} or elsewhere.
research_questions: Can version alerts and ordinary document search answer most routine questions?
Do historical agreement questions reveal recurring scope or exception errors?
Which document formats prevent reliable clause comparison?
new_work: Maintain authoritative versions, effective dates and scope metadata.
Check quoted clauses and review unresolved applicability questions.
Remove superseded interpretation notes from retrieval.
Monitor missed updates and document-comparison failures.

tasks.short: Coordinate customer-related shipments, returns, deliveries and physical handovers with operations and carriers.

steps.what: Review the delivery or return request in the {HELPDESK}.

loop.input: Customer request and linked case fields.
loop.output: Draft shipment requirement with quoted evidence and missing fields.
loop.check: Validate order references and addresses against records; supervisor confirms ambiguous intent.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction; missing or contradictory details require manual clarification.
loop.why_not_simpler: Existing structured fields pass through directly, but customer requests also contain free-text instructions.

steps.what: Check stock, order status and dispatch constraints in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Resolve delivery exceptions with operations, the carrier or the customer.
Create dispatch instructions and assign the handover in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Book the approved carrier service through the {PARTNER_PORTAL}.
Receive or hand over the goods and check their physical condition.
Reconcile handover and carrier status in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.

tasks.design: Connect the {HELPDESK}, {OPS_SYSTEM} and {PARTNER_PORTAL} through deterministic shipment rules and status reconciliation on the {WORKFLOW}. A bounded extraction loop prepares requirements from free-text requests; standard bookings proceed only within approved service, cost and address rules. People handle exceptions and physical handovers, while confirmed status feeds the customer case.
tasks.previous_blocker: Case records, stock status and carrier bookings use different identifiers. Manual re-entry bridges the gaps, while physical checks and delivery exceptions still need people.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing interfaces and inexpensive custom integrations can carry validated identifiers between systems. A small extraction loop helps where requests arrive as free text.
tasks.still_hard: Physical condition, missed collections and disputed delivery promises require local judgement. Carrier interface access, GDPR controls for addresses and reliable retry handling can dominate implementation.
tasks.human_edge: Judge urgency, negotiate recovery options and notice physical problems that records do not show.

ambition.what: Proactive recovery calls for missed customer deliveries

tasks.altitude: The supervisor spends less time chasing status and re-entering bookings, leaving more time for difficult delivery recovery. Existing limits on service promises and spending remain unchanged.

reach.task: Explain shipment exceptions and agree recovery options with customers.
reach.learn: Carrier status meanings, delivery commitments and escalation limits.

reach.task: Coordinate parcel receipt and collection handovers.
reach.learn: Identity checks, condition recording and custody evidence.

evidence.claim: Structured shipment coordination can use deterministic integrations; physical handovers and unusual delivery negotiations remain human.
The supplied digest contains no documented shipment-coordination case; the proposed savings require local validation.

assumptions: The department handles customer replacements, returns or office deliveries involving physical goods.
The task describes the coordinated team process; the supervisor may perform some handovers personally.
Authorised interfaces exist behind the {PARTNER_PORTAL}; otherwise carrier booking remains manual.
Automatic bookings use confirmed addresses, permitted services, cost limits and duplicate-booking protection.
Standard cases can proceed directly; exceptions use the human decision step.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are estimates.
unknowns: Which shipment activities belong to support rather than a separate operations team.
Which carrier interfaces, booking permissions and status feeds are available.
Who may approve address changes, premium services or replacement shipments.
How often requests lack package details or valid order references.
Whether employee tracking is introduced and requires consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which duplicate entries can existing {OPS_SYSTEM} configuration remove?
Can carrier booking support idempotency, cancellation and reliable status matching?
What proportion of coordination time involves physical work or negotiated exceptions?
new_work: Maintain carrier rules, cost limits and identifier mappings.
Resolve failed bookings, unmatched statuses and duplicate events.
Keep address data and handover evidence within retention limits.

role.altitude: The supervisor shifts time from reconciliation, document preparation and status chasing toward service tradeoffs, coaching and exception resolution. Financial, employment and external commitment authority changes only through explicit delegation.
reach: Customer service representatives: connect recurring customer problems to capacity, learning and delivery recovery.
Computer user support specialists: develop accurate troubleshooting practice cases.
Receptionists and information clerks: coordinate reliable physical handovers and receipt records.
skills_to_grow: Diagnosing service problems before prescribing training
Checking source-linked drafts and agreement scope
Managing integration exceptions and external action limits
Applying GDPR, relevant EU AI Act requirements and national consultation rules
role.ambitious_version: Run a support improvement cycle that connects capacity forecasts, targeted learning and delivery recovery, with evidence prepared automatically and consequential decisions made by accountable people.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Office and Administrative Support Workers
